Closes #30050.

- [x] Branched from the latest `origin/develop`; zero conflicts.
- [x] `bun run verify` passed post-sync at head `c9c95fbac6d`: 373 successful, 373 total, exit 0.

# Provider and Model Disclosure

- **Client:** Claude Code
- **Provider:** Anthropic
- **Model:** claude-fable-5-1
- **Attribution status:** self-reported

# Risks

Medium: this adds a cloud database migration (0386) and changes the admission rule of one super-admin operation. The initial selection path is unchanged and still requires an ambiguous inventory; only the explicit re-review boundary accepts a sole remaining candidate, and no request-serving activation or adoption path reconciles anything automatically. The migration is append-only: two nullable columns, one relaxed check, one new check, and one nullable FK with `ON DELETE SET NULL`. The receipt's original audit columns are never rewritten.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Both residuals from #30050, reproduced through the real admin route on PGlite before the change:

1. **Sole remaining candidate trap.** `rereview_existing_personal_dedicated` reused `assertStableAmbiguousInventory`, which throws `PERSONAL_DEDICATED_SELECTION_NOT_AMBIGUOUS` below two candidates. After an owner deleted the non-retained duplicate, the receipt still carried the two-candidate fingerprint, the resolver fell to `unavailable` (it never falls back to `available[0]` while a receipt exists), and the re-review that exists to fix exactly this refused. The database check `candidate_count >= 2` would also have rejected the honest count. A re-review now uses `assertStableRereviewInventory`: the named candidate must be eligible and the inventory within the review bound, nothing more. `assertRereviewChangesReceipt` still refuses a no-op re-review.
2. **Re-reviewing admin not recorded.** The execute path only bumped `updated_at`. It now records `rereviewed_by_user_id` (the acting admin, `null` for the synthetic local-dev admin exactly like `selected_by_user_id`) and `rereviewed_at`, and sets `updated_at` to the same instant; `selected_by_user_id`, `selected_at`, and `created_at` are preserved.

Migration `0386_personal_dedicated_selection_rereview` (journal idx 369, snapshot `meta/0369_snapshot.json`) drops and re-adds the candidate-count check as `>= 1`, adds the two columns, the FK to `users` with `ON DELETE SET NULL`, and a check that an actor implies a time. `drizzle-kit check` reports the journal and snapshots consistent. The PGlite DDL fixture used by the tier-upgrade suites is updated to the same shape.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix with an append-only schema migration.

# Documentation changes needed?

None; the service header and column comments document the boundary.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

`assertStableRereviewInventory` and the receipt update in `packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/personal-dedicated-adoption-selection.ts`, the migration SQL, then the three new cases in `packages/cloud/api/__tests__/admin-personal-dedicated-adoption-selection.pglite.test.ts` (real route, real PGlite, seeded with the suite's own `seedCandidate`/`seedStaleSelection` fixtures) and the new case in the migration PGlite test.

## Detailed testing steps

```bash

bun test __tests__/admin-personal-dedicated-adoption-selection.pglite.test.ts        # 30 pass
bun test __tests__/eliza-agents-adopt-existing-dedicated.test.ts __tests__/eliza-agents-upgrade-tier.test.ts   # 48 pass
bun run typecheck && bun run lint:check
# packages/cloud/shared
bun test src/db/personal-dedicated-adoption-selections-migration.pglite.test.ts     # 4 pass (0319 + 0329 + 0386 applied in order)
bun test src/lib/services/agent-tier-upgrade-target.test.ts src/lib/services/agent-tier-upgrade-target-lock.test.ts   # 21 pass
bun test src/db/migration-journal-registration.test.ts src/lib/services/eliza-sandbox-restore-authority.pglite.test.ts   # 56 pass
NODE_OPTIONS=--require <BigInt toJSON shim> bunx drizzle-kit check                    # Everything's fine

```

Negative control: with `git show origin/develop:.../personal-dedicated-adoption-selection.ts` swapped in and the head tests kept, the three new route cases and the existing fingerprint-drift case (now asserting the actor) fail, 26 pass.

Note on tooling: `drizzle-kit generate` on develop throws `Do not know how to serialize a BigInt` because several schemas use `0n` defaults; generation and `check` were run with a one-line `BigInt.prototype.toJSON` shim via `NODE_OPTIONS`. topPRs.title: fix(lifeops): bind family email approvals and review account replacement
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
## Behavior

Family coordination now supports monthly email drafts bound to the exact sending account, verified recipient, subject, body, and saved version. Owners can edit the email before approval; each save creates an immutable revision and invalidates stale approval. Failed saves retain unsaved text, and downloaded draft records exclude owner-private claims. The UI distinguishes submission for approval from delivery.

The monthly school workflow supports explicit elementary selection and automatic application of validated changes. Identical PDFs produce quiet no-ops, while source configuration and parser-version changes force reconciliation. Live district-PDF inspection exposed preschool and high-school events incorrectly included for elementary families; this change removes those events from existing imports without recreating valid events. Calendar all-day rendering preserves civil dates across time zones.

Google OAuth configuration reaches the runtime, connection errors remain visible, and verified host-session identity reaches plugin access checks. The connection view supports reviewing a replacement account's permissions and synchronized calendars before retiring a selected test account.

## Verification

- Editor revision: 42 focused tests and 68 isolated Chromium checks passed, including saved-version approval, failed-save recovery, exact downloaded text, disclosure filtering, desktop/mobile layout, and hover contrast. Provider adapters in these browser checks are synthetic.
- Full personal-assistant suite at editor commit `30e63ee1960413aa7476bc040dec73774420ab46`: 299 files, 2,569 tests passed, 6 skipped. Root verification passed all 373 tasks and final audits at that revision.
- Calendar package: 840 passed, 4 skipped before the final develop merge.
- School selection and repair: 20 database-backed tests passed. A live DNS-pinned fetch and production PDF parser read the district's current source; the elementary result was inspected against the rendered PDF.
- App audit: 216 OCR-reviewed views, 203 verified, zero broken, 13 needing visual review. Family workspace captures were inspected at four viewports; mobile landscape scroll/overlay acceptance remains open.
- Merged head `2c881a898efb01d3348e7bcc3325f97c7d044078`, including develop `88106f05234d3`: 246 focused school, todo, evaluator, and authored-intent tests passed. Root verification passed (373 successful tasks plus final repository audits). Merge conflicts retain develop's real persistence/owner-isolation coverage and persisted-memory evaluator fixture.

- Final follow-up head `447867a89f947cf1b7495612733cbe4646264f05`: preserve saved calendar selections if account disconnection fails. All 13 account-transition tests passed; root `bun run verify` exited 0 with 373 successful tasks and all final audits. Hosted checks must pass on this revision before merge.

## Remaining release work

This is an incremental implementation PR; full MVP release acceptance remains open. Full operational account cutover (schedules, pending/in-flight approvals, destinations, and test-data disposition), live Google two-way sync and approved email receipts, messaging acceptance, source intake, knowledge-sharing acceptance, current deployment verification, and the final evidence bundle remain open. Account replacement currently verifies connection health; it is not full production handoff acceptance. No provider credentials or private family records are included.

Refs #30123.

topPRs.title: feat(core,discord): FAILURE_REPLY_POLICY keeps canned failure replies out of public rooms
topPRs.author: 0xSolace
topPRs.body:
# Relates to

Follow-up to the addressed-turn failure gate in `MessageProcessor` (the "91 canned-failure sends in 2 days" fix) and the Discord generation-timeout reply. No issue filed; observed live: five "I timed out while generating that reply. Please retry." posts from one agent into a shared guild channel between Sep 6 and Sep 8 during a 29h provider outage.

Definition of Done: [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md).

- [x] Targets `develop`; branched from `357084b3092efb39f95807bcd459baadcc39f095` with no conflicts.
- [x] Frozen install on Bun 1.4.0 / Node 24.14.0; touched-package tests, biome and tsc run after sync.
- [x] Behavioral evidence is included below (before/after test runs on clean develop vs this head).

# Sync with develop

Base is `357084b3092efb39f95807bcd459baadcc39f095` (current `origin/develop` at branch time). No rebase needed.

# Risks

Behavior change with a new default. Under `FAILURE_REPLY_POLICY=dm-only` (default) an addressed turn in a public room that dies before producing a reply now stays silent (error reaction only on Discord) instead of posting a canned failure notice. DMs, VOICE_DM, API, SELF rooms and autonomous turns are unchanged. Operators who want the old behavior set `FAILURE_REPLY_POLICY=all`. Unknown values fail closed to `dm-only` with a one-time warning.

On the Discord group-coordination path the suppressed failure still releases the speaker lease (`state=released`) and writes a `delivery-reconciled` receipt with `outcome=failure-reply-suppressed`, so the crash sweeper does not re-dispatch the edge and other contenders see it close. Covered on the real PGlite path.

Telegram is not touched.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Adds a shared, vendor-neutral `FAILURE_REPLY_POLICY` runtime setting (runtime.getSetting, env fallback) in `packages/core/src/failure-reply-policy.ts`:

- `dm-only` (default): canned failure text only in DM / VOICE_DM / API / SELF rooms and autonomous turns
- `all`: legacy behavior, failure text everywhere
- `off`: never post failure text

Two producers consult it:

1. **core** `MessageProcessor`: the existing deterministic-addressing gate decides *whether the turn addressed the agent*; the policy now decides *whether that room may receive failure text at all*. Suppression logs the existing "suppressing failure reply" pattern with `reason=policy`, `policy`, `policyReason`, `channelType`, and terminates as IGNORE.
2. **plugin-discord** `sendFailureReply` (timeout and provider-error paths): under `dm-only` in a guild channel or thread it still sets the ❌ reaction, aborts the pending draft, runs the inbound-memory release, releases the speaker lease and writes the coordination receipt, but never calls `channel.send`. Logs at info with `code=DISCORD_FAILURE_REPLY_SUPPRESSED_PUBLIC`, `channelId`, `cause` (`timeout` | `provider`).

## What kind of change is this?

Feature with a behavior-changing default, plus regression tests.

# Documentation changes needed?

Setting is documented in the module docblock. No user-facing docs page lists connector env vars for this path yet; happy to add one if maintainers point at the right file.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

`packages/core/src/failure-reply-policy.ts` (the whole policy, ~200 lines), then the two call sites: `packages/core/src/services/message/processor.ts` (structured-failure gate) and `plugins/plugin-discord/messages.ts` (`sendFailureReply`).

## Detailed testing steps

```sh
bun install --frozen-lockfile
# core
bunx vitest run --config packages/core/vitest.config.ts \
  packages/core/src/__tests__/failure-reply-policy.test.ts \
  packages/core/src/services/message.runtime-failure-suppression.test.ts
bunx vitest run --config packages/core/vitest.config.ts packages/core/src/services
# discord
cd plugins/plugin-discord && bunx vitest run
```

Bidirectional proof (same new test files copied onto a clean `357084b3092` worktree, fix absent):

| suite | clean develop | this head |
|---|---|---|
| plugin-discord full (`bunx vitest run`) | 6 failed / 869 passed (875), 2 files | 875 passed (875), 100 files |
| plugin-discord `__tests__/failure-reply-policy.test.ts` | 5 failed / 3 passed | 8 passed |
| plugin-discord `test/messages-group-coordination-pglite.test.ts` | 1 failed / 9 passed | 10 passed |
| core `message.runtime-failure-suppression.test.ts` | 4 failed / 16 passed | 20 passed |
| core `__tests__/failure-reply-policy.test.ts` | n/a (new module) | 15 passed |
| core `packages/core/src/services` sweep + touched runtime tests | not run | 1864 passed (1864), 107 files |

The 3 passing-on-baseline cases in the new Discord file are the legacy-behavior pins (DM keeps reply, `all` keeps reply); the 5 failing ones are exactly the suppression cases. Three existing core tests that pin failure-reply TEXT on an addressed group turn (`message.character-failure-templates`, `message.context-overflow-reply`, `message.credit-exhaustion-reply`) opt into `FAILURE_REPLY_POLICY=all` so they keep exercising the template path; the existing pglite "fences the provider-error reply" test does the same.

Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.63.0

🔒 Test locks

Tests that access a shared resource — an external service, a global account setting — can now declare a named lock. Tests that share a lock name never run concurrently, across files, workers and projects, while everything else keeps running in parallel:

test('update user settings', { lock: 'user-settings' }, async ({ page }) => {
  // never runs at the same time as other tests holding 'user-settings'
});

A test can hold multiple locks, and test.describe() accepts a lock for the whole group. Learn more about test locks.

🪟 Locate across frames

page.frameLocator() and frame.frameLocator() called without a selector search in any frame of the subtree, so you no longer need to locate the iframe first:

// Finds the button in any frame on the page.
await page.frameLocator().getByRole('button').click();

The rest of the locator resolves inside a single frame, just like a regular locator, and an error is thrown when it matches elements in several frames.

👁️ Visible-only locators

New locator.visible() returns a locator that matches only visible elements. It is the recommended replacement for the :visible CSS pseudo-class:

await page.locator('button').visible().click();

🧾 Step params and subtitles

Steps now carry structured data for reporters. Playwright API steps report the target locator and call arguments, and test.step() accepts subtitle and params options for your own steps:

await test.step('Login', async () => {
  // ...
}, { subtitle: 'as admin', params: { user: 'admin' } });

Release notes

Sourced from @​vitejs/plugin-react's releases.

plugin-react@6.1.1

Add compiler.logDiagnostics option

Recoverable React Compiler diagnostics are no longer logged by default. Set compiler.logDiagnostics to true to log them through Vite. Fatal diagnostics are always logged and fail the transform.

Respect environment sourcemap option for React Compiler transform when builder.sharedPlugins is enabled (#1439)

The React Compiler transform was using the top-level sourcemap option instead of the environment sourcemap option. This caused a problem when the experimental builder.sharedPlugins was enabled.

Add experimental native React Compiler support (#1419)

Add experimental native React Compiler support.

You can use it by installing oxc-transform-react and enabling it via the compiler option:

npm install -D oxc-transform-react

import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'

export default defineConfig({

plugins: [

react({ compiler: true })

]

})
